name: Ciarán Walsh
headline: 36, backend engineer, Galway
title: A Quick Call to Help the Intern
situation: On a Tuesday morning, the project lead sends a message to the team chat: the new intern is stuck on a build error that Ciarán fixed last Thursday. The lead suggests, “Ciarán, do you have five minutes to hop on a call and walk her through it?” Ciarán is in the middle of his usual quiet routine—coffee is hot, laptop on the kitchen table. He knows the fix is simple and already documented it. He could reply that he’ll send a note instead, or he could join the call and talk it through. The intern waits, and the lead expects an answer soon.

context.relationship_profiles:
Transactional rapport with the lead, built on short ticket messages.
Intern is a stranger; he knows her name and recurring build errors.
He prefers teammates who rarely need his direct help.
context.tendencies:
When asked in chat, he posts a documentation link and avoids calls.
He joined video calls twice this year, camera off, replies brief.
He attempts unfamiliar problems solo for an hour before consulting anyone.
context.current_state:
Mid-morning, freshly showered, coffee in hand, one task queued.
Mood steady; last week's fix still clear in memory.
No meetings until after lunch, morning feels open.
context.immediate_memories:
Intern's name recalls her Monday build-config query he left unanswered.
The phrase 'hop on a call' reminds him of a summer temp he assisted with a note.
He remembers writing the exact error and the flag that needed resetting.
context.reflective_memories:
He recalls his father fixing a tractor alone, saying explaining took longer than doing.
After the shed collapse, the family avoided neighbourly help; that lesson stuck.
He thinks of the footbridge step he replaces quietly each month, unacknowledged but useful.
